name: The Sanctity and Dignity of Human Life

objectives.text: Identify that God made every person and that every human life is precious to him
Recall the sixth commandment and state that God gave it to protect people's lives
Describe from Psalm 139 how God forms and knows each person before birth
Explain from Genesis 9:6 why taking innocent human life is a grave wrong because people bear God's image
Give examples of how God's law commands kindness and protection toward weak people such as the blind, the deaf, orphans, and widows
Explain the duties the sixth commandment requires for preserving one's own life and the lives of others
Explain why people of every nation and ethnicity have equal worth before God and why showing partiality is sin
Explain how Jesus taught that the sixth commandment forbids sinful anger, hatred, and cursing words as well as murder
Compare the biblical view of human life with practices in ancient and modern cultures that have devalued life, such as infant exposure
Explain from Scripture why the Reformed tradition teaches that a person must care for his or her own body and life rather than harm it
Analyze biblical passages that speak of unborn children as persons known and called by God
Distinguish murder from the taking of life in public justice, lawful war, and necessary defense as the Westminster Standards explain
Classify the duties and sins listed under the sixth commandment in the Westminster Larger Catechism as matters of heart, word, and deed
Describe practical ways believers and the church can obey the biblical call to rescue and speak for those who cannot speak for themselves
Analyze how the early and Reformation church applied the sanctity of life through care for abandoned infants, the sick, and the poor
Evaluate common arguments for abortion against Scripture's teaching on the personhood of the unborn and the sixth commandment
Evaluate arguments for euthanasia and assisted suicide in light of God's sovereignty over life and death
Defend the dignity of people with disabilities, the elderly, and the unborn against views that ground human worth in ability or usefulness
Evaluate contemporary bioethical practices such as embryo destruction and selective genetic screening using biblical principles of human dignity
Create a written Christian ethic of human life that traces human dignity through creation, fall, redemption, and resurrection

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (precious life, sixth commandment, Psalm 139, Genesis 9:6 basis, care for the vulnerable, hatred as murder, unborn personhood, abortion and euthanasia evaluation, defense of the disabled and aged, capstone ethic). Dropped the vague grade 1 and grade 3 restatements of 'life is sacred because of the image' that belong to the Imago Dei sibling, and merged the redundant 'connect image to abortion and euthanasia' and 'construct a pro-life ethic' into the evaluation and capstone objectives. Added equal worth across ethnicities, care for one's own body, the lawful-taking-of-life distinction from WLC Q136, classification of catechism duties and sins, speaking for the voiceless, church history of life-care, and contemporary bioethics. Corrected confession anchors to WSC Q67 to Q69 and WLC Q135 to Q136 and added verse-specific Scripture.
